domain: Enterprise AI System Design & Multi-Agent Architecture
title: Architecting a Multi-Agent Autonomous Workflow for Global Supply Chain Risk Mitigation
context: A global logistics provider wants an autonomous AI system that monitors weather feeds, port congestion news, and supplier inventory, and automatically re-routes shipments when risk thresholds are breached.
dilemma: How do you architect a multi-agent state machine (e.g., LangGraph / CrewAI) with Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) fallback, deterministic transactional execution, and zero infinite-loop failure modes?

must_include: State Machine graph with explicit transition conditions
HITL approval gateway for high-cost re-routings
common_pitfalls: Designing a single monolithic prompt agent
Allowing unvalidated autonomous agent execution of high-value monetary transactions

star_model_answer.situation: A global supply chain client required an AI agent system to detect supply disruption risks and execute shipment re-routing automatically.
star_model_answer.task: Design a resilient, multi-agent enterprise architecture with strict safety and transactional guarantees.
star_model_answer.action: I designed a cyclic graph architecture using LangGraph featuring specialized agents: Monitoring Agent, Impact Evaluator Agent, and Action Execution Agent. I incorporated a Human-in-the-Loop approval node whenever rerouting cost exceeded $10,000, implemented event-driven Kafka messaging, and added state checkpointing in PostgreSQL for full auditability.
star_model_answer.result: The architecture successfully automated 78% of routine disruption mitigation without human intervention while guaranteeing zero unauthorized financial execution.

domain: Enterprise Data Privacy, Guardrails & Security Architecture
title: Preventing PII Leakage & Prompt Injection in Banking AI Customer Assistant
context: A tier-1 retail bank is building an AI financial advisor. Security auditors flag extreme risks of Prompt Injection (Direct & Indirect) and unauthorized PII exposure to third-party LLM APIs.
dilemma: How do you design an enterprise-grade AI Firewall & Guardrail Gateway architecture between the client application and LLM providers?

must_include: Inbound PII masking/tokenization proxy before API call
Prompt Injection classifier (e.g., DeBERTa-v3 guardrail model)
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) tied to vector retrieval
common_pitfalls: Relying solely on LLM system prompt instructions for PII safety
Storing raw customer data in vector embeddings without encryption

star_model_answer.situation: Security auditors halted a bank's AI advisor launch due to vulnerabilities to prompt injection and potential PII leak to cloud APIs.
star_model_answer.task: Architect an enterprise AI Security Gateway enforcing Zero Trust privacy and threat detection.
star_model_answer.action: I architected an inline AI Gateway featuring a dual-pass filter: 1) Presidio PII Anonymizer that tokenizes SSNs and account numbers before leaving the network, 2) NeMo Guardrail pipeline running a fine-tuned BERT prompt-injection classifier, and 3) Vector store RBAC filtering matching user JWT permissions.
star_model_answer.result: Passed 100% of third-party red-team penetration tests, achieved SOC2 & GDPR compliance approval, and enabled secure production launch.
